title: Prairie Avenue's west side, 18th to 20th, stands as a first draft
items: Nine houses and nine coach houses and sheds now stand south of Glessner, from 1812 to 1916, on the outlines traced off the 1911 map.
Each takes its family's roof: mansards for the Second Empire houses, a stepped gable at 1812, a turreted steep roof at 1912, flat cornices on the stone fronts.
Every face is closed and windowed: fronts with stoops, doors and dormers, and coach houses with carriage and loft doors on the alley.
They are drafts, and their cards say so: every height, roof and window is reconstructed, and each names the ticket that will refine it.
